title: Describing things
goal: Describe people and things by colour, size and quality, make adjectives agree, and compare (bigger, the biggest).
intro:
Gujarati adjectives come before the noun. Adjectives ending in **-ઉં / -ો / -ી** change to agree with the noun's gender and number (**સારો** છોકરો, **સારી** છોકરી, **સારું** ઘર), while adjectives ending in other sounds never change (**લાલ** ગાડી, **લાલ** ફૂલ).

Comparison is easy: 'X is bigger than Y' is 'X Y-**કરતાં** big is'.

phrases.native: મારો ભાઈ મારા કરતાં ઊંચો છે.
phrases.roman: māro bhāī mārā kartāṃ ūṃcho chhe.
phrases.en: My brother is taller than me.

grammar.title: Adjective agreement
grammar.body:
Adjectives that end in **-ઉં** in the dictionary change their ending to match the noun, exactly like the possessives મારો/મારી/મારું:

**-ો** masculine singular: મોટો ઓરડો 'a big room'
**-ી** feminine (singular & plural): મોટી બારી, મોટી બારીઓ
**-ું** neuter singular: મોટું ઘર
**-ા** masculine plural (and before postpositions): મોટા ઓરડા; મોટા ઘરમાં 'in the big house'
**-ાં** neuter plural: મોટાં ઘરો

All other adjectives — લાલ, સરસ, સુંદર, ગરમ, ભારે — are **invariable**.

Adjectives used after the verb (as predicates) agree too: ઓરડો મોટો છે, બારી મોટી છે.

grammar.title: Comparison: કરતાં and સૌથી
grammar.body:
Gujarati doesn't change the adjective to compare. Instead:

**Comparative:** X + Y-**કરતાં** + adjective: **આ ઘર તે ઘર કરતાં મોટું છે** 'This house is bigger than that house'. You can add **વધારે** 'more' or **ઓછું** 'less' for emphasis: **વધારે મોંઘું** 'more expensive'.

**Superlative:** **સૌથી** + adjective 'the most': **સૌથી મોટું** 'the biggest'. 'Of all' can be made explicit with **બધામાં**: **બધામાં સૌથી નાનો** 'the youngest of all'.

Pronouns before કરતાં take the oblique/possessive form: **મારા કરતાં** 'than me', **તમારા કરતાં** 'than you'.

examples.native: મારી બહેન મારા કરતાં લાંબી છે.
examples.roman: mārī bahen mārā kartāṃ lāmbī chhe.
examples.en: My sister is taller than me.
I'm the youngest in the family.

dialogue.title: Choosing a sari
dialogue.setting: Pooja and her mother look at saris for a cousin's wedding.

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.native: મમ્મી, આ લાલ સાડી કેવી છે?
lines.roman: mammī, ā lāl sāḍī kevī chhe?

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: સુંદર છે, પણ થોડી ભારે છે.
lines.roman: sundar chhe, paṇ thoḍī bhāre chhe.
lines.en: It's beautiful, but a bit heavy.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: એ લાલ કરતાં હલકી છે. રંગ પણ સરસ છે.
lines.roman: e lāl kartāṃ halkī chhe. raṅg paṇ saras chhe.
lines.en: That's lighter than the red one. The colour is nice too.

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.native: પણ મને લીલી વધારે ગમે છે.
lines.roman: paṇ mane līlī vadhāre game chhe.
lines.en: But I like the green one more.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.en: The green one is the most expensive!

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.native: હા, પણ એકદમ સુંદર છે, ને?
lines.roman: hā, paṇ ekdam sundar chhe, ne?
lines.en: Yes, but it's really beautiful, isn't it?

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.en: OK, OK. Take the green one.

culture: Colours carry meaning in Gujarat: red and green are auspicious for weddings and festivals, while white is worn for mourning. The traditional Gujarati wedding sari is the white-and-red **પાનેતર** *pānetar*, and the **ઘરચોળું** *gharcholuṃ* is a red or green checked silk sari given by the in-laws.
